title: Last Plank
designBriefSource: The requested six-family planning batch; private prompt retained outside distribution.
goal: Collect the western gem while retaining the blue shield through the final gate.
stageDependency: Spend the access plank -> recover the blue and retained floor -> assemble the northbound convoy -> independently translate the floor to form a westbound convoy -> fill the gap floor-first -> reuse blue for the final gate.
planningBurden: One resource is irreversible, both modules must remain operable through a turn, and actor order decides whether the blue survives.
changedConstraints: Two purposeful bridge resources replace the source multi-chamber allocation network.
One narrow gate throat makes shared delivery causally necessary.
A compact turning bay exposes the difference between independent reassembly and a nonexistent object rotation.
physicalScope: One 16 by 16 room; ordinary pinned official engine; all initial actors at elevation zero.

difficulty.qualification: An author estimate from dependent operations and planning tradeoffs, not calibrated human difficulty.

limits: Both planks, blue motion, actual convoy contact, final floor consumption and the ordered blue reuse pass exhausted exclusions.
The blue-first loss is demonstrated from ordinary reachable states; no arbitrary actor swapping is used.
Exact floor positions and every turn translation are not claimed uniquely necessary.
